verses.zh: 尼布甲尼撒王晓谕住在全地各方、各国、各族的人说：「愿你们大享平安！
verses.en: (3:31)[NOTE:1] King Nebuchadnezzar, to all peoples, nations, and language groups that live in all the land: “Peace and prosperity![NOTE:2]
notes: Beginning with 4:1, the verse numbers through 4:37 in the English Bible differ from the verse numbers in the Aramaic text (BHS), with 4:1 ET = 3:31 AT, 4:2 ET = 3:32 AT, 4:3 ET = 3:33 AT, 4:4 ET = 4:1 AT, etc., through 4:37 ET = 4:34 AT. Thus Dan 3:31-33 of the Aramaic text appears as Dan 4:1-3 in the English Bible, and the corresponding verses of ch. 4 differ accordingly. In spite of the division of the Aramaic text, a good case can be made that 3:31-33 AT (= 4:1-3 ET) is actually the introduction to ch. 4.
Aram “May your peace increase!”

verses.zh: 我乐意将至高的　神向我所行的神迹奇事宣扬出来。
verses.en: I am delighted to tell you about the signs and wonders that the most high God has done for me.

verses.zh: 他的神迹何其大！他的奇事何其盛！他的国是永远的；他的权柄存到万代！
verses.en: “How great are his signs! How mighty are his wonders! His kingdom will last forever,[NOTE:1] and his authority continues from one generation to the next.”
notes: Aram “His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom.”

verses.zh: 「我尼布甲尼撒安居在宫中，平顺在殿内。
verses.en: (4:1)[NOTE:1] I, Nebuchadnezzar, was relaxing in my home,[NOTE:2] living luxuriously[NOTE:3] in my palace.
notes: This verse marks the beginning of chap. 4 in the Aramaic text of Daniel (see the note on 4:1). The Greek OT (LXX) has the following addition: “In the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign he said.” This date would suggest a link to the destruction of Jerusalem in 586 b.c. In general, the LXX of chapters 4-6 is very different from the MT, so much so that the following notes will call attention only to selected readings. In Daniel 4 the LXX lacks sizable portions of material in the MT (e.g., vv. 3-6, 31-32), includes sizable portions of material not in the MT (e.g., v. 14a, parts of vv. 16, 28), has a different order of some material (e.g., v. 8 after v. 9), and in some instances is vastly different from the MT (e.g., vv. 30, 34). Whether these differences are due to an excessively paraphrastic translation technique adopted for these chapters in the LXX, or are due to differences in the underlying Vorlage of the LXX, is a disputed matter. The latter seems more likely. There is a growing trend in modern scholarship to take the LXX of chapters 4-6 much more seriously than was the case in most earlier text-critical studies that considered this issue.
Aram “my house.”
Aram “happy.”

verses.zh: 我做了一梦，使我惧怕。我在床上的思念，并脑中的异象，使我惊惶。
verses.en: I saw a dream that[NOTE:1] frightened me badly. The things I imagined while lying on my bed—these visions of my mind—were terrifying me.
notes: Aram “and it.”

verses.zh: 所以我降旨召巴比伦的一切哲士到我面前，叫他们把梦的讲解告诉我。
verses.en: So I issued an order[NOTE:1] for all the wise men of Babylon to be brought[NOTE:2] before me so that they could make known to me the interpretation of the dream.
notes: Aram “from me there was placed a decree.”
The Aramaic infinitive here is active.

verses.zh: 于是那些术士、用法术的、迦勒底人、观兆的都进来，我将那梦告诉了他们，他们却不能把梦的讲解告诉我。
verses.en: When the magicians, astrologers, wise men, and diviners entered, I recounted the dream for them. But they were unable to make known its interpretation to me.

verses.zh: 末后那照我神的名，称为伯提沙撒的但以理来到我面前，他里头有圣神的灵，我将梦告诉他说：
verses.en: Later Daniel entered (whose name is Belteshazzar after the name of my god,[NOTE:1] and in whom there is a spirit of the holy gods). I recounted the dream for him as well,
notes: This explanation of the meaning of the name Belteshazzar may be more of a paronomasia than a strict etymology. See the note at 1:7. The king's god was Marduk, who was called Bel (“Lord”).

verses.zh: 『术士的领袖伯提沙撒啊，因我知道你里头有圣神的灵，甚么奥秘的事都不能使你为难。现在要把我梦中所见的异象和梦的讲解告诉我。』
verses.en: saying, “Belteshazzar, chief of the magicians, in whom I know there to be a spirit of the holy gods and whom no mystery baffles, consider[NOTE:1] my dream that I saw and set forth its interpretation!
notes: The present translation assumes the reading חֲזִי (khazi, “consider”) rather than the MT חֶזְוֵי (khezve, “visions”). The MT implies that the king required Daniel to disclose both the dream and its interpretation, as in chapter 2. But in the following verses Nebuchadnezzar recounts his dream, while Daniel presents only its interpretation.

verses.zh: 「我在床上脑中的异象是这样：我看见地当中有一棵树，极其高大。
verses.en: Here are the visions of my mind[NOTE:1] while I was on my bed. “While I was watching,there was a tree in the middle of the land.[NOTE:2] It was enormously tall.[NOTE:3]
notes: The LXX lacks the first two words (Aram “the visions of my head”) of the Aramaic text.

Instead of “in the middle of the land,” some English versions render this phrase “a tree at the center of the earth” (NRSV); NAB, CEV “of the world”; NLT “in the middle of the earth.” The Hebrew phrase can have either meaning.
Aram “its height was great.”

verses.zh: 那树渐长，而且坚固，高得顶天，从地极都能看见，
verses.en: The tree grew large and strong.Its top reached far into the sky;it could be seen[NOTE:1] from the borders of all the land.[NOTE:2]
notes: Aram “its sight,” as also v. 17.
Or “to the end of all the earth” (so KJV, ASV); NCV, CEV “from anywhere on earth.”

verses.zh: 叶子华美，果子甚多，可作众生的食物；田野的走兽卧在荫下，天空的飞鸟宿在枝上；凡有血气的都从这树得食。
verses.en: Its foliage was attractive and its fruit plentiful;on it there was food enough for all.Under it the wild animals[NOTE:1] used to seek shade,and in its branches the birds of the sky used to nest.All creatures[NOTE:2] used to feed themselves from it.
notes: Aram “the beasts of the field.”
Aram “all flesh.”

verses.zh: 「我在床上脑中的异象，见有一位守望的圣者从天而降。
verses.en: “While I was watching in my mind’s visions[NOTE:1] on my bed,a holy sentinel[NOTE:2] came down from heaven.
notes: Aram “the visions of my head.”

Aram “a watcher and a holy one.” The expression is a hendiadys, as also in v. 23. This “watcher” is apparently an angel. The Greek OT (LXX) in fact has ἄγγελος (angelos, “angel”) here. Theodotion simply transliterates the Aramaic word (ʿir). The term is sometimes rendered “sentinel” (NAB) or “messenger” (NIV, NLT).

verses.zh: 大声呼叫说：『伐倒这树！砍下枝子！摇掉叶子！抛散果子！使走兽离开树下，飞鸟躲开树枝。
verses.en: He called out loudly[NOTE:1] as follows:[NOTE:2] ‘Chop down the tree and lop off its branches!Strip off its foliageand scatter its fruit!Let the animals flee from under itand the birds from its branches.
notes: Aram “in strength.”
Aram “and thus he was saying.”

verses.zh: 树墩却要留在地内，用铁圈和铜圈箍住，在田野的青草中让天露滴湿，使他与地上的兽一同吃草，
verses.en: But leave its taproot[NOTE:1] in the ground,with a band of iron and bronze around it[NOTE:2] surrounded by the grass of the field.Let it become damp with the dew of the sky,and let it live with[NOTE:3] the animals in the grass of the land.
notes: Aram “the stock of its root,” as also in v. 23. The implication here is that although the tree is chopped down, it is not killed. Its life-giving root is spared. The application to Nebuchadnezzar is obvious.

The function of the band of iron and bronze is not entirely clear, but it may have had to do with preventing the splitting or further deterioration of the portion of the tree that was left after being chopped down. By application it would then refer to the preservation of Nebuchadnezzar’s life during the time of his insanity.
Aram “its lot be.”

verses.zh: 使他的心改变，不如人心；给他一个兽心，使他经过七期（期：或译年；本章同）。
verses.en: Let his mind[NOTE:1] be altered from that of a human being,and let an animal’s mind be given to him,and let seven periods of time[NOTE:2] go by for[NOTE:3] him.
notes: Aram “its heart.” The metaphor of the tree begins to fade here and the reality behind the symbol (the king) begins to emerge.
The seven periods of time probably refer to seven years.
Aram “over” (also in vv. 23, 25, 32).

verses.zh: 这是守望者所发的命，圣者所出的令，好叫世人知道至高者在人的国中掌权，要将国赐与谁就赐与谁，或立极卑微的人执掌国权。』
verses.en: This announcement is by the decree of the sentinels;this decision is by the pronouncement of the holy ones, so that[NOTE:1] those who are alive may understand that the Most High has authority over human kingdoms,[NOTE:2] and he bestows them on whomever he wishes.He establishes over them even the lowliest of human beings.’
notes: The present translation follows an underlying reading of עַל־דִּבְרַת (ʿal divrat, “so that”) rather than MT עַד־דִּבְרַת (ʿad divrat, “until”).
Aram “the kingdom of man”; NASB “the realm of mankind”; NCV “every kingdom on earth.”

verses.zh: 「这是我―尼布甲尼撒王所做的梦。伯提沙撒啊，你要说明这梦的讲解；因为我国中的一切哲士都不能将梦的讲解告诉我，惟独你能，因你里头有圣神的灵。」
verses.en: “This is the dream that I, King Nebuchadnezzar, saw. Now you, Belteshazzar, declare its[NOTE:1] interpretation, for none of the wise men in[NOTE:2] my kingdom are able to make known to me the interpretation. But you can do so, for a spirit of the holy gods is in you.”
notes: The present translation, as also in the next verse, reads פִּשְׁרֵהּ (pishreh, “its interpretation”) with the Qere and many medieval Hebrew MSS; the Kethib is פִּשְׁרָא (pishraʾ, “the interpretation”).
Aram “of.”

verses.zh: 于是称为伯提沙撒的但以理惊讶片时，心意惊惶。王说：「伯提沙撒啊，不要因梦和梦的讲解惊惶。」伯提沙撒回答说：「我主啊，愿这梦归与恨恶你的人，讲解归与你的敌人。
verses.en: Then Daniel (whose name is also Belteshazzar) was upset for a brief time;[NOTE:1] his thoughts were alarming him. The king said, “Belteshazzar, don’t let the dream and its interpretation alarm you.” But Belteshazzar replied, “Sir,[NOTE:2] if only the dream were for your enemies and its interpretation applied to your adversaries!
notes: Aram “about one hour.” The expression refers idiomatically to a brief period of time of undetermined length.
Aram “my lord.”

verses.zh: 你所见的树渐长，而且坚固，高得顶天，从地极都能看见；
verses.en: The tree that you saw that grew large and strong, whose top reached to the sky, and that could be seen[NOTE:1] in all the land,
notes: Aram “its sight.”

verses.zh: 叶子华美，果子甚多，可作众生的食物；田野的走兽住在其下；天空的飞鸟宿在枝上。
verses.en: whose foliage was attractive and its fruit plentiful, and from which there was food available for all, under whose branches wild animals[NOTE:1] used to live, and in whose branches birds of the sky used to nest—
notes: Aram “the beasts of the field” (also in vv. 23, 25, 32).

verses.zh: 「王啊，这渐长又坚固的树就是你。你的威势渐长及天，你的权柄管到地极。
verses.en: it is you,[NOTE:1] O king! For you have become great and strong. Your greatness is such that it reaches to heaven and your authority to the ends of the earth.
notes: Much of modern scholarship views this chapter as a distortion of traditions that were originally associated with Nabonidus rather than with Nebuchadnezzar. A Qumran text, the Prayer of Nabonidus, is often cited for parallels to these events.

verses.zh: 王既看见一位守望的圣者从天而降，说：『将这树砍伐毁坏，树墩却要留在地内，用铁圈和铜圈箍住；在田野的青草中，让天露滴湿，使他与地上的兽一同吃草，直到经过七期。』
verses.en: As for the king seeing a holy sentinel coming down from heaven and saying, ‘Chop down the tree and destroy it, but leave its taproot in the ground, with a band of iron and bronze around it, surrounded by the grass of the field. Let it become damp with the dew of the sky, and let it live with the wild animals, until seven periods of time go by for him’—

verses.zh: 「王啊，讲解就是这样：临到我主我王的事是出于至高者的命。
verses.en: this is the interpretation, O king. It is the decision of the Most High that this has happened to my lord the king.

verses.zh: 你必被赶出离开世人，与野地的兽同居，吃草如牛，被天露滴湿，且要经过七期。等你知道至高者在人的国中掌权，要将国赐与谁就赐与谁。
verses.en: You will be driven[NOTE:1] from human society,[NOTE:2] and you will live[NOTE:3] with the wild animals. You will be fed[NOTE:4] grass like oxen,[NOTE:5] and you will become damp with the dew of the sky. Seven periods of time will pass by for you before[NOTE:6] you understand that the Most High is ruler over human kingdoms and gives them to whomever he wishes.
notes: The Aramaic indefinite active plural is used here like the English passive, as also in vv. 28, 29, and 32.
Aram “from mankind,” as also in v. 32.
Aram “your dwelling will be,” as also in v. 32.
Or perhaps: “be made to eat.”

Nebuchadnezzar’s insanity has features that are associated with the mental disorder boanthropy, in which the person so afflicted imagines himself to be an ox or a similar animal and behaves accordingly.
Aram “until.”

verses.zh: 守望者既吩咐存留树墩，等你知道诸天掌权，以后你的国必定归你。
verses.en: They said to leave the taproot of the tree, for your kingdom will be restored to you when you come to understand that heaven[NOTE:1] rules.
notes: The reference to heaven here is a circumlocution for God. There was a tendency in Jewish contexts to avoid direct reference to God. Compare the expression “kingdom of heaven” in the NT and such statements as: “I have sinned against heaven and in your sight” (Luke 15:21).

verses.zh: 王啊，求你悦纳我的谏言，以施行公义断绝罪过，以怜悯穷人除掉罪孽，或者你的平安可以延长。」
verses.en: Therefore, O king, may my advice be pleasing to you. Break away from your sins by doing what is right, and from your iniquities by showing mercy to the poor. Perhaps your prosperity will be prolonged.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Aram “if there may be a lengthening to your prosperity.”

verses.zh: 这事都临到尼布甲尼撒王。
verses.en: Now all this happened[NOTE:1] to King Nebuchadnezzar.
notes: Aram “reached.”

verses.zh: 过了十二个月，他游行在巴比伦王宫里（原文是上）。
verses.en: After 12 months, he happened to be walking around on the battlements[NOTE:1] of the royal palace of Babylon.
notes: The word “battlements” is not in the text but is supplied from context. Many English versions supply “roof” here (e.g., NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV); cf. NLT “on the flat roof.”

verses.zh: 他说：「这大巴比伦不是我用大能大力建为京都，要显我威严的荣耀吗？」
verses.en: The king uttered these words: “Is this not the great Babylon that I have built for a royal residence[NOTE:1] by my own mighty strength[NOTE:2] and for my majestic honor?”
notes: Aram “house.”
Aram “by the might of my strength.”

verses.zh: 这话在王口中尚未说完，有声音从天降下，说：「尼布甲尼撒王啊，有话对你说，你的国位离开你了。
verses.en: While these words were still on the king’s lips,[NOTE:1] a voice came down from heaven: “It is hereby announced to you,[NOTE:2] King Nebuchadnezzar, that your kingdom has been removed from you!
notes: Aram “in the mouth of the king.”
Aram “to you they say.”

verses.zh: 你必被赶出离开世人，与野地的兽同居，吃草如牛，且要经过七期。等你知道至高者在人的国中掌权，要将国赐与谁就赐与谁。」
verses.en: You will be driven from human society, and you will live with the wild animals. You will be fed grass like oxen, and seven periods of time will pass by for you before[NOTE:1] you understand that the Most High is ruler over human kingdoms and gives them to whomever he wishes.”
notes: Aram “until.”

verses.zh: 当时这话就应验在尼布甲尼撒的身上，他被赶出离开世人，吃草如牛，身被天露滴湿，头发长长，好像鹰毛；指甲长长，如同鸟爪。
verses.en: Now in that very moment[NOTE:1] this pronouncement about[NOTE:2] Nebuchadnezzar came true.[NOTE:3] He was driven from human society, he ate grass like oxen, and his body became damp with the dew of the sky, until his hair became long like an eagle’s feathers and his nails like a bird’s claws.[NOTE:4]
notes: Aram “hour.”
Or “on.”
Aram “was fulfilled.”
The words “feathers” and “claws” are not present in the Aramaic text, but have been added in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 日子满足，我―尼布甲尼撒举目望天，我的聪明复归于我，我便称颂至高者，赞美尊敬活到永远的　神。他的权柄是永有的；他的国存到万代。
verses.en: But at the end of the appointed time[NOTE:1] I, Nebuchadnezzar, looked up[NOTE:2] toward heaven, and my sanity returned to me.I extolled the Most High, and I praised and glorified the one who lives forever. For his authority is an everlasting authority, and his kingdom extends from one generation to the next.
notes: Aram “days.”
Aram “lifted up my eyes.”

verses.zh: 世上所有的居民都算为虚无；在天上的万军和世上的居民中，他都凭自己的意旨行事。无人能拦住他手，或问他说，你做甚么呢？
verses.en: All the inhabitants of the earth are regarded as nothing.[NOTE:1] He does as he wishes with the army of heavenand with those who inhabit the earth.No one slaps[NOTE:2] his handand says to him, “What have you done?”
notes: The present translation reads כְּלָא (kelaʾ), with many medieval Hebrew MSS, rather than כְּלָה (kelah) of BHS.
Aram “strikes against.”

verses.zh: 那时，我的聪明复归于我，为我国的荣耀、威严，和光耀也都复归于我；并且我的谋士和大臣也来朝见我。我又得坚立在国位上，至大的权柄加增于我。
verses.en: At that time my sanity returned to me. I was restored[NOTE:1] to the honor of my kingdom, and my splendor returned to me. My ministers and my nobles were seeking me out, and I was reinstated[NOTE:2] over my kingdom. I became even greater than before.
notes: The translation reads הַדְרֵת (hadret, “I returned”) rather than the MT הַדְרִי (hadri, “my honor”); cf. Theodotion.
The translation reads הָתְקְנֵת (hotqenet, “I was established”) rather than the MT הָתְקְנַת (hotqenat, “it was established”). The MT could read: “And regarding my kingdom, it was established.”

verses.zh: 现在我―尼布甲尼撒赞美、尊崇、恭敬天上的王；因为他所做的全都诚实，他所行的也都公平。那行动骄傲的，他能降为卑。
verses.en: Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise and exalt and glorify the King of heaven, for all his deeds are right and his ways are just. He is able to bring down those who live[NOTE:1] in pride.
notes: Aram “walk.”
